table.title: Русский / Tiếng Việt · Diacritics
table.md:
| Термин | Tiếng Việt | Описание |
|---|---|---|
| Производительность | Hiệu năng | Способность системы обрабатывать запросы с минимальной задержкой при высокой нагрузке. |
| Масштабируемость | Khả năng mở rộng | Возможность увеличивать ресурсы без изменения архитектуры. |
| Отказоустойчивость | Khả năng chịu lỗi | Hệ thống vẫn tiếp tục hoạt động khi một hoặc nhiều thành phần gặp sự cố. |

understanding.purpose: A Russian–Vietnamese terminology table pairs technical terms with translations and explanations.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the Russian term and its Vietnamese equivalent together, then read across the row for the explanation. Wrapped text should remain clearly associated with its row.
groups: Columns 1 and 2 form the terminology pair: Russian terms and their Vietnamese equivalents.
Column 3 provides explanatory prose for each pair.
keep_intact: Russian terms, including the 134px unbreakable term
may_wrap: Vietnamese multiword equivalents at word boundaries
Descriptions at natural word boundaries; their longer prose will generally set the row height

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: Keep both terminology columns on one line and give the remaining space to descriptions for straightforward row-by-row lookup.

preferred.name: r1A
preferred.note: Keep the strongest tested balance: both terminology columns fit their longest entries on one line, leaving the remaining width for descriptions.

acceptable.name: r0B
acceptable.note: Allow Vietnamese phrases to wrap to give descriptions the most space, using the height already needed by longer explanations.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Give Russian terms more breathing room and Vietnamese phrases moderate space, accepting more wrapping in the descriptions.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give 11px from the Vietnamese column to the descriptions, testing whether a modest wrap in an equivalent buys more comfortable prose without disrupting the terminology pair.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Test a slightly narrower Vietnamese column and a wider description measure as a middle ground between r0A and r0B.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The first column has only 99px of text space, forcing the 134px Russian term to split within the word. The extra space in the Vietnamese column does not compensate for that loss of readability.
bad.why: The first column has only 99px of text space, forcing the 134px Russian term to split within the word. The extra space in the Vietnamese column does not compensate for that loss of readability.

rationale: r0A and r1A are identical. They keep both the Russian terms and Vietnamese equivalents on single lines, making the paired terms easy to scan, while giving the longer descriptions enough room to form readable lines. The narrower Vietnamese columns in the other candidates wrap two equivalents without reducing the table's height.

general: Give columns enough space to preserve important words and identifiers intact.
Judge width changes by how they affect scanning and the balance of the whole table, not only by table height.
specific: The Vietnamese equivalents fit on one line at 132px including padding, so that width supports comparison across the two term columns.
All candidates have the same row heights, making their differences in wrapping and space distribution more consequential than compactness.

tradeoffs: A designer may prefer r0B's wider description column for its longer lines, accepting wrapped Vietnamese equivalents. r0C gives the Russian terms more breathing room but leaves less space for descriptions and wraps the equivalents.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates around the preferred allocation, not browser-verified breakpoints. They describe one column varied at a time with the remaining width shared proportionally; exact line breaks can shift at nearby widths.

critique.good: The Russian terms and Vietnamese equivalents remain intact on single lines, making each pair easy to scan. The description has a readable measure, and the rows remain clear.
critique.problems: The Vietnamese column has some spare space that could give the prose a little more room.
critique.cause: At 132px, column 2 is wider than needed for its 111px longest line plus 21px of padding and borders.

critique.good: The Russian terms remain intact, and the wider description column gives the prose a more comfortable measure.
critique.problems: Two Vietnamese equivalents wrap, weakening the quick comparison between the paired terms without reducing the height of any row.
critique.cause: At 90px, column 2 provides only 69px of text width; the space saved is assigned to the 322px description column.

critique.good: The Russian terms have ample room, and the table remains easy to follow across rows.
critique.problems: Two Vietnamese equivalents wrap while conspicuous spare space sits beside the Russian terms. The narrower description column also makes the prose feel more compressed.
critique.cause: Column 1 is 190px wide despite needing 155px to fit its longest term; column 2 is 112px and column 3 is 265px.

critique.good: The Russian terms and Vietnamese equivalents each stay on one line, making the terminology pairs easy to scan. The descriptions wrap naturally, and the rows remain clear units.
critique.problems: The first description takes three lines, leaving some white space beside the shorter terminology pair, but the row remains easy to read.
critique.cause: The 280px description column must accommodate substantially longer prose than the other columns.

critique.good: The Russian terms remain intact, and the descriptions have slightly more room.
critique.problems: Two Vietnamese equivalents wrap, weakening the quick visual pairing with the Russian terms. The added description width does not reduce any row height.
critique.cause: The 121px Vietnamese column provides only 100px for text, less than the 111px needed by the longest equivalent.

critique.good: The Russian terms remain intact, and the description column is the widest of the three designs.
critique.problems: Two Vietnamese equivalents wrap, while the descriptions and row heights show no corresponding improvement. The terminology pair is less compact to scan than in r1A.
critique.cause: The 115px Vietnamese column provides 94px for text; the extra width given to the description column does not change the observed line counts.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: The Russian terms break within words, making the first column difficult to scan despite a generous description column.

r0A.why: Russian terms and Vietnamese phrases remain intact, while the descriptions have enough width to wrap naturally. The columns feel well balanced for their roles.

ref_auto.why: The Russian terms stay intact and descriptions read comfortably, though the narrow Vietnamese column splits two short phrases across lines.

ref_equal.why: Both term columns stay on one line, but they take space from the descriptions, which wrap into narrow blocks and make the rows taller.

r0B.why: The wide description column reads comfortably and Russian terms stay intact, but the narrow Vietnamese column splits two phrases across lines.

r0C.why: The description column is reasonably wide, but the Vietnamese phrases wrap awkwardly, leaving short final lines; the first column has more space than it needs.

raw.unsure: C and E are close: both trade Vietnamese phrase width for a wider description column.

r0B.why: Russian terms stay intact and the description has ample space. Two Vietnamese entries wrap, but the rows remain easy to scan.

r0A.why: Both term columns keep their entries intact, while the descriptions wrap naturally. The three columns have a clear, useful balance.

contrast.why: The narrow first column breaks each Russian term within the word, making the labels harder to read and compare.

ref_auto.why: Russian terms stay intact and the description column is generous. Two Vietnamese entries wrap, though the rows still read clearly.

r0C.why: Russian terms stay intact, but the first column has more space than it needs while two Vietnamese entries wrap and the descriptions are tighter.

ref_equal.why: The two term columns have substantial spare space, leaving the descriptions narrow and fragmented across many lines. The resulting tall rows weaken scanning.

raw.unsure: A and D are very close; their small width differences have little effect on readability.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
